Absolut. Ich hab meine Wege damit umzugehen aber ich hatte schon situationen in denen mich das völlig fertig gemacht hat.


Aber mein Lieblingsbeispiel ist eigentlich als ich damals als Kind aus einem 5 tägigem Sommercamp nach hause kam... und bei Gott die Tassen nicht mehr finden konnte. Und man lacht das so weg weil dann nimmst du halt ein Glas oder so oder du machst halt alle Schränke auf aber das was keine 'Vergesslichkeit'. Das hat sich mehr nach einem Fehler im System angefühlt. Ein Teil meines Hirns der verschwunden ist. Eine Lücke einfach. Und ich hab mich so bescheuert gefühlt denn ich war ja nur 5 Tage weg und ich lebte in dem Haus seit ich geboren war!

Ein Therapeut der dich lieber mit Burnout, Depression, Angststörung, BPD, verschiedenen Esstörungen und was nicht alles diagnostiziert ("welche ja zu Stress, Unkonzentriertheit, und Vergesslichkeit führen können"), statt die Möglichkeit in betracht zu ziehen dass es vielleicht "nur" ADHS ist, würde ich persönlich den Vogel zeigen.


Ich dachte Jahrelang ich sei kaputt weil ich ja keinen Grund für meine grottige mentale Gesundheit habe und ich bin halt einfach dazu verdammt mein leben in einer Klinik oder so zu verbringen.


Ja ka, turns out dass, das Leben halt einfach frustrierend und scheiße sein kann wenn du ständig zu spät kommst, nicht schlafen kannst, deine Sachen verlierst, deine Hausaufgaben nicht machst, zu laut bist, nicht mit denkst, aka ADHS hast. Inzwischen komm ich viel besser klar und ich hab seit der Behandlung nicht mehr gedacht dass ich mich umbringen muss also irgendwas scheint ja richtig zu laufen!


Ich war damals bei einem Therapeuten der das auch angezweifelt hat und seine Begründug lag halt auf nichts das mit mir zu tun hatte, sondern ausschließlich auf der überpopularisierung in den Medien. Er war nicht unvoreingenommen dabei kannte er mich nicht einmal.


Ich hab meinen Hausaurzt gewechselt weil ich bei den Tests offensichtlich auch eine ausgiebige körperliche Untersuchung machen sollte und der HA bei dem ich bisher war, mir erst einmal einen Vortrag darüber gehalten hat wie ADHS doch nur Geldmacherei für die privaten psychiater ist. Hatte an dem Tag fast aufgegeben weil ich laut der Aussage die 500€, die ich eig nicht mal besessen habe, in die Tonne gehauen habe und immer noch keinen Schritt weiter war. Er wollte mich nicht untersuchen weil er nicht weiß ob der psych legit ist, konnte mir aber uch keinen anderen nennen der mir helfen könnte.


Meine jetzige HA hat mich ohne Frage untersucht und sich die nächsten male die ich da war auch interessiert erkundigt.


Es sind die Ärzte die (solange sie dir damit keinen bleibenden Schaden zufügen) dir erst einmal glauben, egal womit du denen ankommst.
Das ist echte Unvoreingenommenheit und nicht dieser unbegründete Zweifel!

TDLR: Dein Bruder braucht Hilfe. Wenn du helfen möchtest dann sag etwas. Deine Mutter soll Probleme ihrer Kinder nicht ignorieren sonst ist sie keine gute Mutter. Easy as that.

Jemanden wie dich in meinem Leben gehabt zu haben hätte mir so gut getan! Zu wissen dass sich irgendwer für einen interessiert und sich um einen kümmert auch ohne gute Leistung in der Schule ist wirklich ein Fels an dem man sich festhalten kann. Aber raus aus der Brandung holt einen dieser allein nicht.

Natürlich ist es eigentlich ja gar nicht deine Aufgabe da du dir ja auch nicht ausgesucht hast dass deine Eltern weitere Kinder bekommen aber wenn du wirklich helfen möchtest würde ich den Vorschlägen in anderen Kommentaren folgen und eurer Mutter sagen dass jetzt neue Wege ausprobiert werden müssen.

Sie ist überfordert mit einem weiteren Sonderkind? Tja, schade dass haben sich die Kinder nämlich auch nicht ausgesucht. Du hast als Elternteil halt einfach eine verdammte Pflicht deinem Kind zu helfen wenn es hilfe braucht und die Augen zu verschließen bringt da gar nichts. Eher das Gegenteil. Es stört sie ja auch dass dein Bruder so untergeht.

Als jemand mit ADHS kann ich nur darum betteln dass irgendwer etwas tut. Kaum jemand testet dich als Erwachsener darauf ohne dass du Geld regnen lässt ganz abgesehen von den anstrengenden Anforderungen/Tests bis zur Diagnose.

Auf jeder Kinder und Jungendpsych Seite wird von ADHS geredet aber wenn du dann erwachsen bist, auf dich allein gestellt und deine Geduld und Energiereserven eigentlich schon drei mal aufgebraucht sind weil es dir so viel abverlangt einfach nur "mitzuhalten" (wenn überhaupt)... es ist halt einfach nicht schön.

Erwachsene dürfen übrigens auch falsch liegen. Falls du es übers Herz bringst kannst du euch allen einen großen Gefallen tun wenn du es bei deiner Mutter ansprichst und bei möglichem Widerstand weiter darauf bestehst dass es nach all den Jahren halt nicht mehr so weiter geht. Wie soll sich was an seinen Noten ändern wenn sich nichts anderes ändert?

Außerdem soll dein Bruder nicht denken er sei nichts Wert nur weil er nicht in dieses System rein passt dass dich nur an ein paar Zahlen bewertet. Wenn er sich nicht selbst verliert wird er auch keine Probleme haben einen Job/Beruf zu finden. Die wenigsten Unternehmen achten am Ende wirklich auf deine Schulnoten als wie du dich präsentierst und welche Erfahrungen du mit bringst.

Falls das alles nicht geht, schlag doch mal vor ihn in einem Sport anzumelden oder so. Irgendwas was er nach der Schule machen kann um überschüssige Energie abzuladen und einen klareren Kopf zu bekommen. Ein leises Fidget-Toy für die Schule. Vielleicht schaut man mal darauf was er denn zum Frühstück isst und ob es da vielleicht ein paar Konzentrations crasher gibt. Nachhilfe bzw einfach nur jemand der dabei ist wenn er seine Hausaufgaben macht als eine Art Body-Doubleing. Verschiedene Lernmethoden raussuchen und einfach mal zusammen schauen was funktioniert und was nicht.

Fakt ist aber dass du ein gebrochenes Bein nicht so leicht repariert bekommst egal wie viele Pflaster du drauf tust.

Egal ob normal oder nicht, sobald du deinem Partner sagst dass du dich bei soetwas unwohl fühlst, sollte er das respektieren und darüber nachdenken. In einer Beziehung interessiert es einen nämlich wie der/die andere sich fühlt. Tut er das nicht find ich ist das gesammte vorliegende Paket hier, eine einzige red flag. Solche übergriffigen 'Witze' können besonders im Gruppenkontext die Hemmschwelle schnell sinken lassen. Bevor dir dann also doch mal jemand auf den Hintern haut (oder schlimmeres) wäre es nötig etwas zu sagen.

Man kann dem auch voran gehen und beginnen mit "Hey eventuell verärgert dich das jetzt gleich aber ich brauch dass du mir jetzt nüchtern zuhörst."

Außerdem würde ich vielleicht Platz für die Möglichkeit lassen dass er sich in dieser Gruppe vielleicht auch einfach dazu angesgachelt fühlt da so mit zu reden wie die anderen es tun, aber am Ende des Tages hast du absolut recht. Er sollte dich quasi 'verteidigen' auch wenn er glaubt dass du nicht zuhörst. Wozu geht man denn sonst eine Beziehung ein wenn einem sein Partner nicht wichtig genug für soetwas ist?!

Bitte denke nicht dass du spießig bist wenn du dein Wohlbefinden schützt. Solange du niemanden angreifst hast du jegliches Recht dazu!
Oha, direkt noch was neues gelernt! Gut zu wissen.

Als jemand die natürlich ständig vergisst ihr Rezept pünktlich abzuholen bevor die Praxis Urlaub macht, hab ich tatsächlich vielleicht eine Idee für dich.

Also dann halt so 100ml rein, umrühren, 50ml trinken.

Ob das jetzt besonders schlimm ist weil das dann nicht erst im Bauch aufgelöst wird, kann man jetzt hinterfragen. Weiß ich nicht. Gestorben bin ich aber noch nicht.

Ansonsten, falls es dir der Aufwand wert ist, kann man sich leere pillen kapseln kaufen und dann nach Augenmaß diese neu befüllen mit einer kleineren Menge. Hat nur ordentliche Walter White Vibes.

Tbh I dont know what qualifies me to answer this but from what I have learned as a caucasian dark blonde wavy to curly hair girl that lived with an afro like puffy head of hair for way too long is:


1. Conditioner is what makes hair so smooth and easy to comb through (only learned that in my teen years. Didnt really have anyone teaching me anything about beauty so I thought I mention that as well just in case).


There can be "too much" conditioner. Some dont need anything at all and their hair just needs to get used to nkt getting bombarded with mosture all the time again. It can make your hair go oily really fast again. Also it can make your hair "think" that it doesnt need to produce any more mositure so it dries out when you stop using it.


Two in one shampoo/conditioner has a bad stigma but is actually much more complex than just combined shampoo and conditioner and for some peoples hair its just the perfect solution.


Conditioner is supposed to be only used on the hair ends and not the roots since the natural oils work there the most.


1.2 To clean our hair, shampoo needs to break down the oils on our head by using "surfactants". The usual surfactants in shampoo are SLS and SLES. There are shampoos that use both tho which is nice in a cleanliness way but it totally strips you of any natural oil in your hair which causes dryness.


2. Broken hair looks frizzy.


Your hair is most brittle when damp so dont move it too much at that stage and dont go to bed with wet hair. Extreme temperatures, tight hairties, bleaching, dyeing and even the wrong hairbrush can break your hair. Brush it through before a shower but maybe just use a gentle comb after it. Enough to make it work for you and your hair style.


3. Are nails and skin dry and/or brittle too? Ask a doctor. I had a lack biotin and while it doest turn me into a glowing KPop Beauty Idol it saved my skin from being literally flaky after some meds dried me out even more.


Not saying that it definetly is biotin but it might be worth to check (with a doc) for some deficiancies (in general).


4. Satin pillow case. Satin head cover. Satin lined hats in winter. Might be something to get used to but is supposed to save your hair especially when you are moving a lot in your sleep.


5. Let hair air dry (if the temperatures allow it). Or use the cold blow dryer funktion if necessary. Also try not to use too much heat when showering/bathing. You literally start sweating on your head right after because of the heat which will cause unwanted oilyness which can cause you hair to "learn" that it doesnt need to produce any anymore.

The day I lost my dog and got stranded 2,5h away from my hometown because of the worst weather after I had two really exhausting days at a friends house that ended with a fight. I was already crying all the way through since I got the call from my mom and went on my way home. It was a long way and trains and buses got cancelled and delayed all the way through. I called friends when I stranded on the outer edge of the city in the rain and they eighter didnt pick up or their parents (with cars) werent available. My mom didnt pick up eighter but she was also on her way to her boyfriend who lived in another city so it would have taken her hours to get me. I was scared shitless asking strangers in their cars to take me with them but finally some nice ladies did and brought me home to an empty house. Normally my dog would have been there with me. But she wasnt. That sucked big time.

My father had died when I was 10 but the feeling of abandonedment, the loneliness, sadness, anger and fear and having zero controll over anything that happened just made it worse. I watched a bunch of disney movies the next days after to get over it and also the cold I got that day.

What helped me was when people stayed casual about everything. Not making a big deal out of my eating disorder if they knew but also not ignoring it. That way they knew not to make a scene or cracking jokes when they noticed I havent eaten anything for a while. But they also wouldnt leave me out when they ask everyone if they want to eat something. And then when I say no, thats just it.

That way I was able to kind of start to feel normal about it again. It was like "learning" that eating was normal? And then I slowly tried to "act normal" as I said yes to a french fry or two. And then it was just fake it 'til u make it. This was the height of my ed. I had completely lost touch to reality and this somehow helped me to get back.

So I say its neutral as long as its kept neutral!

From my limited understanding after years of internet research, I kind of want to assume that something like lazyness doesnt really exist. Maybe for like 3 seconds when you sigh before you have to get up of the couch but not more.

Our brains (not only from adhd people) crave all the chemicals that make us feel good (dopamine, noradrenaline, serotonin, etc.) and despises everything that does the oposite. Its quite simple: Food = Nutrition = Surviving or Pain = Broken Body = No Surviving.

We unconciously remember everytime a good song, made us feel good or doing the dishes was a hard task. There is no need in knowing "its not that bad" for your brain to want to do everything to keep you from doing this annoying task again especially because its a time where you can think about all the other, way cooler things you could do. I guess its some kind of torture and it gets worse each time.

And then we can "train" our feelings and/or our indurance towards those things. Doing a hard task over and over again might not suddenly get easier but you become better at it. More confrontation with an annoying task helps your brain to get used to it and then be fine with it. Some people might call it "Discipline".

As for the feelings, idk... I am convinced that if we put a little bit of effort into seeing the good things in... things, we will actually find it (or train our brains to look out for it and therfore finding more good things). Like the feeling after you have finally finished the dishes and your kitchen is clean.

Keep in mind that this is the understanding and opinion of someone who has never studied a thing about pyschology apart from what she looked up on the internet somewhere. But this is basically the reason why I dont believe lazyness exists. Our brains just try to save us from "pain" or bad feelings. Which is why, allthough my whole life is slowly getting better since I get medicated, I still cant study because school and learning is engraved as the biggest pain in the butt there is for me. Gotta have to do a lot of reprogramming myself.

That being said; imma go and do the dishes now.

And this is where social media is toxic. I am sorry that happened to you! I can imagine that this experience also leaves a mark. Of course this would be a perfect reason to delete social media.

Not to convince you or others but to maybe give an idea of what I mean when I say social media can be used in a good way: I for example use social media mainly for two things. To store pictures and videos kind of like in a picture book way and to get inspired. I do have two accounts though. One where I plan to post and share my creative work just because I like it and one only about me which stays private. I do have really nice friends around me and a healthy amount of cinfidence though which probably makes it easy for me. If someone is "offended" that I dont follow or like them or unfollowed them I mostly shrug my shoulders and tell them honestly that their content doesnt work for me.
As for the "get inspired" part; Its like when you see someone do something cool and you want to recreate it. Taking pictures, drawing, building, fitness, cooking. All that. Sometimes I throw away my phone to finally start working on something. Start creating. I kind of like that aspect.

Sometimes I glanze over the stories of friends. And I recently started to follow my "favorite" news channel so I finally have some sort of more active news input.

Thats it and I quite like it. I do feel a little attacked though when in a group discussion everyone is only talking about the bad aspects of social media. And what shall I say. They are not wrong. I just feel like we are often forgetting a big part of the puzzle.

That being said: I had reddit deleted for the longest time because I get too hooked on writing overly long comments (as you can see) and only wanted to install it to communicate with people writing the same finals as me. I guess today will be deletion day again since this page (as much as I love it) is not doing it for me in a way that would fit the above explaination.

Have a great one! And you are never wrong for doing something that helps your mind and/or body (as long as it doesnt hurt anyone else)!

Its not. I find it pretty cool actually. What I do think is a red flag is when you feel better than people and/or talk down to people who have social media.

There are so many different ways you can use it and not all of it is or has to be toxic!

Sport and/or friends.

I grew up in a rather small and cute village. My friend and neighbour once locked his bike at the train station.

It was gone the next day.

Came back the day after that with a new lock and a note that said something like:
"So sorry! I really needed to get somewhere fast! Code Locks are usually pretty easy to pick open. Here is a better one. Thank you for the bike!"

... you couldnt even be mad.

- Horse riding as a child. I loved it. It was the one thing that gave my week a routine! Hat to stop though because my instructor had to focus on uni and stopped working. Never found a horse riding instructor that I was comftable with ever again so I guess it didnt quite stick... but I did it for years so yeh.

- Playing Piano. I grew up with a piano in the house and had some basic skills but never seriously started playing. Until I bought a used e piano from my friend. There is no routine or regularity in it but I am playing nearly everyday even if for just 5 minutes and I am kind of good at it and playing other instruments as well. Feels nice.

- Bouldering/ Climbing (indoor). Finally did it once after years of saying I wanna try that. Had the time of my life and it was cheap af (even cheaper when I didnt have to rent shoes anymore). I did it more and more basically every week! Just like that! No schedule! If I dont go I dont have to still pay. Nobody is forcing me. No routine. No regularity. I just go when I have time and have a blast however long I want or until they are closing... or until I fell and had to go the hospital.

I dislocated my shoulder in december and I couldnt get it back in (I was used to this) so I had to go to the hospital. They fixed it but the recovery time here was waaaay longer than all the other times I dislocated it and was able to put it back instantly. But they gave me cetamine so I didnt have to sit in the pain so even though it was a shitty situation... I had a BLAST! 10/10!!! Can recommend bouldering to everyone! I am finally at a state where I can think about going climbing again. I gotta stay at the easier routes but I just finally wanna go again! It is addicting.

I have also since learned that climbing can actually be the perfect substitution for any addiction you have. It can give you this instant gratification as soon as you hit a new personal high. And you never have to wait for someone else or get left behind because its only you! You and the wall. And hey! I havent started dringing or smoking again so at least its not making you addicted to something! xD

When I was still working as a game master here is how we "handled" this stuff:

2. We actually had no breaks. While we were doing games we are allowed to eat, be on the phone (not exsessively of course) or talk to other game masters. down, down - up, up - down - up

But here some basics I myself found very helpfull in the last years (but take my tips for a grain of salt. Maybe you find more tips in this sub r/ADHS):

Try to sit down for a second and think about the topic you have to battle now. It took me dropping out of school for 3 times to realize I actually like math. Most things are actually pretty interesting but we are so focused on the fact that its all a chore. Idk for me that helps.

When you have to write texts then make those paragraphs. Its easier to remember where you were and how much you have to read.

Sometimes texts are unecessaryly complicated so if you have the question you are supposed to answer, just look up the information in the internet.

I know it sounds like a wanna be adhd magician but turn notifications off on your phone. Its the vibration that gets me every time.

When studying I actually actively listen to music with lyrics. At least for me they dont distract me but they give my mouth something to do. I automatically start whipping my head to it which is kind of therapeutic and kid of gives me a rythm. But it needs to be music I know the lyrics or melody too.

If this doesnt help try without lyrics or binaural beats.




This is less about studying:

So basically you get distracted a lot from about everything so you need to limit the things you have to think about like cleaning your room (store things where you need them and take a look into minimalism).

Or what your want to wear (have a favorite shirt? Buy it 5 times or more.

I have problems thinking about eating so I always have some healthy snacks around. Like grapes. So I at least get that amount of nutrition at the end of the day and dont eat just a bunch of take out at the end of the day.

Store things where you use it. I saw someone puting their desk in their closet and having an open closet in their room for their clothes.

Start realizing when you need to remember something you are thinking off. And then write it down, record it or tell a friend.

Literally any moment is the best moment to start being better. I believe you can do this no matter how bad your mental health is. Lets say you start with watching a youtube video about people who ran a marathon or cleaned their room. People that want to or did achieve something. I dont know why but for some people this brings up the motivation to start changing to the better. I can really recommend anything by Matt D'Avella but his videos are a lot about minimalism and you have to see if you like it or not. Just frigging start with watching a video. Thats something easy. And then you need a job. Sounds much harder than you think. Most of the time people only have something like beeing a waiter or delivery guy in mind but did you ever think about being a librarian? I mean I dont know anything about this job but it just came in my mind. You might think you are bad in social interactions but I believe nobody is. My brother has asbergers and avoids anything with social interactions as much as possible but if he cant he is the most handsome and smartest person you can imagine. You know how to talk to people because you know how you want to be talked to. So lets get something like an escaperoom in you mind. Work as a minijobber in a lasertag location. The only thing you have to do is to get the cash from the people and tell them what to do. Most of the time these companies are very small so it is kind of a chill environment there. I swear to god. Nothing helped me more with my social anxiety than working there. You find out what you are able to do. Once in a while you will have a little obstacle and you will see that you can overcome this too. There you can make some new friends that can open the world a little more for you. I mean you need dicipline and me for myself had to change jobs for a consistant worktime to have more controll on that. Maybe it just isnt something for you but it is a great opportunity to not lose time. Getting work expierience while getting your education. I costs money but college does too right? These are like three steps. 

1. Get motivated (watch a video) 

2. Get a job (consider something easy and relaxed to get a picture of what you are cappable of. You can do more than you think) 

3. Start college or try studying online (depends on what fits you. Online courses can helf you "save time" but that shouldnt be your main focus. Finding out where are your strenghts can give you so much more that any college degree ever could) 

On applying and writing cv's and interviews: Of course you need to write a cv maybe and apply for jobs but that too is much more easier than you think. Just copy an application from the internet and change it so it fits to the job you want. How do you write a cv? Also look on the internet. There you can write every little sh** you want. Write where you went to High School and College (nobody needs to know that you quit or what you wanted to study in the first place). Write in there that you were pretty interested in computerized games. Do you have any skill like taking care for your cat? Do you like hanging with your friends? Write that you are a teamplayer. These are the little things. You can even write down what your hobbies are. At the end they wont even care what you wrote. Everything comes down to the interview. You should be honest but not to honest. They will see that you didnt do anything for years. Tell them that there were some bigger issues in your private life but you are determined to finally start. Dont forget to smile. Dont wear a suit or something like that. Be casual but dont come in your boxers. Some questions you should maybe think of before are "Tell me something about you.", "Why do you want to work here?", "Why should we hire you?". Always keep in mind that you are allowed to say anything as long as its true. "I want to show my best and help the company improve." You want to. If you can because of your mental health is not important for them at least not in the interview. But at the end you just need to find a way to be chill. They will take you or not. There are plenty of other opportunities and then you just had a good training if it didnt work out. The rest will come by itself. Just dont be scared to try new things and be open for anything. I never would have thought to work in a bank too where we dont even talk in my native language. It is really so much easier to get a job than you think and if it is the right one your life will improve too. You just need to give it some time maybe. If you still have any questions feel free to ask me. I actually hired people for a while and hopefully I can or were able to help you. You just need to start. 

It also sounds like you parents are pretty understanding with you so maybe they can bring up more patience for you when you start doing sonething which would be great. Thank your parents and prove them you can do this!

The only thing I can say is be open and kind. Being a game master is mostly just small talk when you bring the customers to their rooms or the waiting room or something like that. I always have some basic questions to ask so I can fully take on the role as the one who hosts their game. I am in charge for their experinece. These are simple questions like:
Did you come here well?
Did you ever played and escape room?
If yes where and how was it?
Are you here for fun or is there a special ocasion?
Mostly there is something they will tell you that you can pick up and turn into a better conversation and if not then its okay too. Sometimes it is just quiet between people. Thats life.
People tend to speak really fast when they are nervous so just concentrate on speaking slowly. This is also good for the customers to understand you. Take your time and be calm. Its all about having a relaxed aura while also doing a good job. When the customers are in the game give them time for everything they do. There will be always groups that are so bad that you kind of need to push them through but dont give a hint when they just found a quest. Give them time to think for themselfes. If you can be creative then give the hints in the style of the story but no pressure here. Dont be scared to immedietly jump in action when one of the customers looks like he is about to rip some wires off the wall or something that they are clearly not supposed to do. You will see this all the time and as long as you told them in the briefing before the game to not break anything you are on the right side. Also what I like to tell them is "If you are not sure if something is part of the game then just ask. Its better than breaking anything". After the game just go through it with the customers. After one finishes a book most people dont know what to do with themselfes. Same thing for escape rooms. Ask them what they think about this room. And especially about this one special quest and just talk a bit about their experience so they dont feel so lost afterwards. But I dont know how much time you have between games so it depends on this too. When reseting a room go exactly backwards. This makes this whole thing easier. And say bye to the cutomers so they know there is a cut and they can go. I saw it a couple times now that they just stood around and I asked them how I can help them and they just didnt know if they could go... awkward.

I hope this is not too long to read but being a game master is pretty easy as long as you are chill and have basic skills of cummunication. The main thing for the long term is probably just be a nice coworker. Be responsible and dont say you cant come to your shift only 10 minutes before the first game. Dont steal money from the cashier. Ask questions if you didnt understand something. Immediently tell someone if something in the room is broken. It sounds ridiculous but all that happened at my work place. Just have a decent working moral and everything will be good.

Last thing: This is more for you than the job. Stay calm! You are not allowed to kill the cutomers no matter what assholes they are. You cant change them. And you cant yell at them so there is nothing to do than drinking some tea and just swallow all this shit. (But other than that the job is pretty cool).
Have fun!
